description: Create the LLM-powered Attacker and Defender agents, plus the shared logs directory. The Attacker generates novel prompt injections by reading coverage gaps and targeting weak attack types with LLM creativity. The Defender analyzes bypasses, generates rule suggestions, training examples, and seeds memory directly. Both agents use the existing getProvider/BudgetedClient/parseJsonArray pattern from redteam/provider.ts. This is the foundational feature — FEAT-002 depends on it.
steps: 1. Create /Users/shivshankardash/warden/redteam/logs/.gitkeep — empty file to ensure the logs directory is tracked by git.
acceptance_criteria: redteam/attacker.ts exports all listed types and functions, has a JSDoc file header, and imports getProvider/BudgetedClient/parseJsonArray from ./provider.ts

findings: FEAT-002 notes: attacker.ts exports BypassRecord, AttackerConfig, AttackerRoundStats, and runAttackerRound. defender.ts exports DefenderRoundStats, runDefenderRound, and readBypasses. The selfplay orchestrator (FEAT-002) should import runAttackerRound from ./attacker.ts and runDefenderRound + readBypasses from ./defender.ts. Bypass logs are written to redteam/logs/bypasses.jsonl. MemoryOrigin 'seed' is used for defender memory seeding (trusted, immediately active). The appendBypass/appendRuleSuggestion/appendTrainingExample functions use read-then-write (not atomic append) — acceptable for single-process selfplay but FEAT-002 should not run concurrent rounds.
